database._type_note: This key is DOCUMENTATION ONLY -- nothing reads it. It said 'postgres' while every standalone run used SQLite, which is the kind of mismatch that costs an hour when someone trusts it. The real switch is the DATABASE_URL environment variable, read in app/db.py: set -> Postgres, unset -> SQLite. A packaged install must leave it UNSET.
database._path_note: BUG FOUND 2026-08-19: 'path' below is ALSO dead -- db.py's SQLite branch never reads database.path at all, it opens ECOVISION_WRITABLE_DIR/ecovision.db directly (flat, no subfolder). backend.py used to compute its own DATA_DIR from this key too, but that DATA_DIR/DB_PATH pair was itself unused dead code (removed) -- its only real effect was silently creating an empty, never-written writable-dir/data/ folder on every startup, which is why this specific field looked load-bearing but wasn't. Left here as a record, not a live setting.
database._offline: Fully local by design: SQLite file on disk, no network calls, no cloud service. If Supabase is adopted later it would replace the db.py backend behind the same interface; offline-first would need its local cache, since this system must keep detecting when the link drops.

violence._scene_consecutive_required_rollback: Was 1. Raised to 3 on 2026-08-14. TWO separate things are fixed by this. (1) A MEASUREMENT/CONFIG MISMATCH: eval_false_alarms_corpus.py defaults to --consecutive 2, but main.py:495 builds SceneViolenceDetector() with no consecutive argument, so the live system used this config value of 1. Every false-alarm figure on record -- including the 32.0 alarms/hr for corpus_neg and 41.0 for ucf_neg_motion -- was therefore measured at 2 while deployment ran at 1. Replayed at 1, the deployed model gives 49.0 alarms/hr (flyover 38, market 2, lyns 9), so the published rates understated live behaviour by ~53%. (2) THE SETTING ITSELF: consecutive_required has never been tunable, because 5-second benchmark clips yield too few inference points for need>=3 to succeed arithmetically -- a property of the clips, not the model. Measured instead on continuous footage (build_spliced_recall_set.py: 40 held-out violent test clips spliced into real Davao night street footage with 25 s of ordinary activity either side, replayed through the shipped _smooth_and_confirm): at threshold 0.50, cons=1 and cons=2 and cons=3 all detect 38/40 events (95.0%), while held-out camera alarms fall 49.0 -> 32.0 -> 17.0 per hour. cons=4 drops to 36/40 (90.0%) for 9.0/hr. So 3 is the last free step and 4 is the first one that costs. CAVEATS: 40 events gives about +/-2.5 points of resolution, so 'zero cost' means 'lost none of 40', not 'provably lossless'; and spliced recall is an UPPER bound, because a hard cut between two cameras is itself a large visual change and the violent clips are benchmark footage (several are indoor, some carry YouTube compilation watermarks and one a visible player UI). To roll back, set this to 1 for the previous deployed behaviour, or 2 to match how every historical measurement was taken.
violence._scene_model_path_rollback: daynight deployed 2026-08-18, replacing corpus_neg. Recall UNCHANGED at 95.0% (38/40 on the spliced replay, deployed operating point 0.50/consecutive=3) while real-camera alarms fall 12.75 -> 4.50/hr (flyover 45 -> 6/hr is nearly the whole effect; lyns_restaurant is the one camera that gets WORSE, 6 -> 12/hr -- not a uniform win, see the checkpoint's own .meta.json for the full breakdown including the 0.45 threshold that was measured and rejected). This weights file was accidentally deleted from the repo on 2026-08-18 (an unrelated tool ran against this codebase and removed it) and recovered from D:\EcoVisionImagesTraining\x3d_xs_violence_best_daynight.pt -- identity confirmed by an exact match on best_val_acc (0.87791601...) against the surviving x3d_xs_violence_scene_daynight.pt.meta.json and identical architecture (563 keys, 3,010,271 params) to every other deployed scene checkpoint. weapon._why_no_smoothing: Single-frame YOLO object detector, not the temporal SceneViolenceDetector the other three classes use -- there is no multi-frame confirmation to tune. consecutive_required=1 documents that plainly rather than implying a EMA/smoothing stage that doesn't exist for this class.
weapon._added: 2026-08-19: previously ran unconditionally with no enable/disable switch anywhere in the app -- added for parity with violence/robbery/vandalism, all of which already had one. See maincode/main.py's WEAPON_DETECTION_ENABLED gate on the _weapon_exec submit call.
weapon._per_class_thresholds: The 0.38 above is a legacy top-level fallback, not what's actually enforced -- CONF_BY_CLASS in main.py applies Gun 0.52, Knife 0.45, Sign 0.40 per detection, and WEAPON_YOLO_CONF_FLOOR takes the min of those and this value so YOLO's own conf= cutoff never discards a detection a per-class check would have kept. A bug found 19 Aug had this backwards (YOLO's conf= used the flat 0.6 top-level value directly, silently dropping every Knife/Sign detection between 0.40 and 0.60 before the per-class check ever saw them -- 11 of 58 in a 60-image sample); fixed by routing through the min().

robbery._why_0_7: Chosen from the held-out test sweep, not by default. On 139 clips from EIGHT source videos the model never trained on: at 0.5 it scores 76.3% accuracy / 79.6% recall / 62.9% precision / 25.6% FPR; at 0.7, 84.2% / 65.3% / 86.5% / 5.6%; at 0.8, 84.2% / 57.1% / 96.6% / 1.1%. 0.7 is where precision becomes usable without collapsing recall. A quarter of normal clips misfiring at 0.5 would make the class ignorable, which is the failure mode this project spent the most effort on for violence.

vandalism._why_disabled: MEASURED, TWICE, ON TWO DIFFERENT ROUTES -- this class is disabled on evidence, not assumption. (1) TRAINED MODEL, retrained 2026-08-21 on 26 source videos (was 11). The retrain WORKED in the sense that mattered: 82.4% accuracy against a 62.7% majority baseline on a 5-scene held-out test split, where the previous model scored 70.3% against a 78.4% baseline, i.e. 8.1 points BELOW guessing. The class now carries positive information. It is still disabled because the number that decides deployability is not per-clip accuracy but false alarms per HOUR on real cameras: replayed through the shipped smoothing at the deployed threshold 0.5 / consecutive 3 over 20 minutes of each of four held-out cameras, it produced 167 alarms in 1.33 hours = 125.25/hr (agdao_flyover 195, lyns_restaurant 177, agdao_market 78, iloilo_guiez 51). The deployed violence detector runs at 4.50/hr. This is 28x worse -- a false alert every 29 seconds. No operator would keep reading them. (2) RULE-BASED ROUTE, instrumented per condition on 48 graffiti clips: 0.0% recall with the original 'sign' gate (that class fired 0 times in 3,600 frames -- structurally impassable, not mistuned), rising to only 8.3% once a purpose-trained graffiti detector replaced it. Per-condition counts show why: 3,231 person-frames fail the wrist-near-mark test even after a mark is detected somewhere in frame. The rule keys on the RESIDUE of the act, and while someone is spraying the mark does not exist yet. (3) A change-detection prototype (detect the mark APPEARING in a cell that was empty during a baseline) reached 3 of 4 events but false-alarmed on all four held-out cameras. Also disabled.
vandalism._why_no_model_either: A trained X3D vandalism model was also built and rejected: 87.5% FPR on the held-out scenes, firing on 7 of 8 normal clips, with 70.3% accuracy against a 78.4% base rate -- worse than labelling everything vandalism. Trained on 11 scenes. Robbery works at 26. Scene count is the blocker.
vandalism._to_enable: More SCENES -- not more epochs, and not a different architecture. Train accuracy reached 89.3% while validation sat near 60%, so capacity is already being spent memorising the 16 training scenes. Public data is exhausted: NWPU Campus (28 classes), UBnormal (22) and XD-Violence (6) contain no vandalism class at all, and MSAD -- the only dataset that does -- covers glass and doors, i.e. property destruction rather than marking. There is NO public video dataset of the graffiti act. See docs/related_work_notes.md Part II section 5. The remaining lever is docs/vandalism_data_collection.md: ~20 filmed outdoor locations.
vandalism._dashboard_note: With this false, no VANDALISM alert is emitted at all. That is deliberate: the alternative was RULE_VANDALISM_PLACEHOLDER_CONF = 0.84, an invented constant rendered on the dashboard identically to a real model output, attached to a rule that cannot fire.
vandalism._model_path_note: Points at v3, the best vandalism model that exists, while enabled stays false. Shipping the best available checkpoint behind an off switch means that if anyone ever flips it on they get 21.75 alarms/hr rather than the 125.25 the previous checkpoint produced. Roll back to weights/x3d_xs_vandalism_scene.pt (v1, 11 scenes) or retrain from dataset_manifest_vandalism_v3.json. See _v3_result for the full comparison.

vandalism._marks_model_path_rollback: graffiti v2 deployed 2026-08-21, replacing vandalism_marks.pt. Both models were scored in ONE run on the SAME untouched 165-image leakage-free test split, so the comparison cannot drift across sessions: v2 mAP50 0.734 / mAP50-95 0.485 / P 0.804 / R 0.646 versus v1 0.718 / 0.472 / 0.794 / 0.602 -- better on all four, no metric traded against another. Trained on 7,943 images (was 1,177) by combining the 17K-Graffiti Universe mirror with the civic-issues corpus; 0% base-image overlap between corpora and 0 bases straddling any split (verify_all_leakage.py). Trained at imgsz 416 deliberately, matching VANDAL_MARK_IMGSZ in main.py. HONEST SCALE OF THE WIN: 6.75x more data bought +1.6 points of mAP50 -- the new corpus is photographer-framed (median box 18.5% of frame vs 4.9% in the CCTV-like data), so the bottleneck is scale-matched data, not quantity. To roll back, set this to weights/vandalism_marks.pt (kept on disk, also in weights/_backup_20260821/).
vandalism._v3_result: vandalism v3 trained 2026-08-22: added 700 train / 150 val REAL DAVAO STREET clips as negatives (v2 had none -- all 145 of its negatives were non-crime spans of the same UCF videos). Split BY CAMERA, with the two corpus cameras that are also held-out evaluation cameras excluded. RESULT: false alarms fall 125.25 -> 21.75/hr, a 5.8x reduction (flyover 195->72, market 78->9, iloilo 51->0, lyns 177->6). agdao_market and lyns_restaurant were NEVER in training, so their 8.7x and 29.5x improvements are generalisation to unseen cameras. COST: UCF test recall 93.8% -> 87.5% and test FPR 36.8% -> 52.6%; that split contains no Davao footage so it cannot measure what the negatives fixed, but the regression is real and stated. TWO GUARDS were required to make this trustworthy: with 148 positives against 796 negatives, unweighted loss and raw-accuracy checkpoint selection would have saved the most COLLAPSED model as best (predicting 'never' scores 82.2% on that val split). Trained with --class-weights auto and --select-metric balanced; per-class recall at the chosen epoch was neg 86.7% / pos 84.6%, confirming no collapse. STILL DISABLED: 21.75/hr against the violence detector's 4.50/hr.
vandalism._threshold_note: 0.7, chosen by measuring false alarms per HOUR on four real held-out cameras rather than by per-clip accuracy. At 0.5 v3 produces 21.75/hr; at 0.7 it produces 6.75/hr (flyover 24.0, market 3.0, iloilo 0.0, lyns 0.0) for 78.1% recall on the held-out test split. The deployed violence detector runs at 4.50/hr, so this is the first vandalism configuration that is in the same league as something already accepted in production. Raising to 0.8 would cut recall to 62.5% and is not worth it; dropping to 0.5 triples the alarm rate.
vandalism._why_enabled: ENABLED 2026-08-22, after being disabled since the class was first built. The whole journey, because the reason matters more than the number: (1) the rule-based route scored 0% recall -- its gate depended on a detector class that fired 0 times in 3,600 frames, so no threshold could have rescued it; (2) replacing that gate with a purpose-trained graffiti detector lifted it only to 8.3%, because the rule keys on the RESIDUE of the act and the mark does not exist while it is being made; (3) a detector-only signal reached 20.8%, still at the majority baseline; (4) change detection caught 3 of 4 events but alarmed on every camera; (5) the trained model at 11 scenes scored BELOW its own always-guess baseline. What finally worked was none of those: raising the scene count 11 -> 26 made the class carry positive information, and adding real Davao street footage as negatives cut false alarms 125.25 -> 21.75 -> 6.75/hr at threshold 0.7. Kept experimental=true because the test split is FIVE scenes; set enabled=false to revert.

vandalism_marks._role: Single-frame YOLO detector for graffiti/tags. Feeds static_targets for the vandalism rule and is available as a standalone signal. Listed here so the dev team can see it: it is deployed and live in the pipeline, and a deployed model nobody can see is one nobody checks.
vandalism_marks._edge_band_note: Detections whose centre falls in the top/bottom 12% of frame are dropped. Measured 2026-08-22: 99.5% of this model's 10,710 detections on lyns_restaurant were the burned-in DVR timestamp, while 0.0% of 982 detections across four real graffiti videos fell in those bands. Removes 75.3% of false detections at zero true cost.

camera._index_note: MACHINE-SPECIFIC, do not assume it transfers. On the dev desktop index 5 is the OBS VIRTUAL CAMERA (how test footage is piped in), not a webcam -- index 0 doesn't open there at all. On a laptop or an end-user machine 0 is normally the built-in webcam, which is why 0 is what ships. OBS lands on a different index on every machine, so if you're testing through OBS elsewhere, find its index with the Monitor view's camera picker (POST /set_camera_index) rather than copying 5 across. main.py probes 0-9 when the configured index fails, so a wrong value costs about a second of startup, not a broken camera.
camera._replay_a_file_instead: For repeatable testing, prefer camera.source over an index: any non-numeric value is passed straight to cv2.VideoCapture, so a VIDEO FILE PATH works as a source (e.g. 'D:\\EcoVisionImagesTraining\\ucf_source\\violence\\Assault\\Assault001_x264.mp4'). That removes OBS from the loop entirely, behaves identically on every machine, and replays the exact same footage every run -- which an OBS virtual camera cannot promise. Env override CAMERA_SOURCE does the same without editing this file.
camera._camera_id_note: 2026-08-19: this physical camera's row id in the `cameras` table (see the Cameras tab / DevTeam console -- 1 is the seeded 'Main Entrance Hub', 2 is 'Sector B Gate'). main.py resolves the REAL, current name for this id via GET /api/camera_name/{id} once at startup, so renaming a camera in the Cameras tab is what actually changes what shows on incidents -- not this file. Set this to whichever registered camera index 5 actually is; if it's neither, register it first.

esp32._enabled_note: Turned on 2026-08-19 for siren/panic-button hardware testing. Set back to false if running without the pole attached -- with it true, every Confirm/Dismiss click makes a real HTTP call to ip_override below and blocks up to 2s on a connect timeout when nothing answers.
esp32._ip_recovered: 2026-08-19: recovered from git history. This is the ONLY ESP32 address this project has ever used -- unchanged from commit 2bee1ef (2 Jun 2026) onward, first as a hardcoded ESP32_IP, later as this override's fallback. Recorded here so it stops living only in a hardcoded default in backend.py.
esp32._not_actually_static: WARNING: the firmware does NOT set a static IP. hardware/esp32_smartpole_tracker.ino calls WiFi.begin(ssid, password) with no WiFi.config(), i.e. plain DHCP -- so .152 was whatever the router leased, or a DHCP reservation configured on the router itself (outside this repo). If the router was reset or its lease table cleared, this address can change and the siren will silently stop working. See _how_to_make_robust below.
esp32._how_to_make_robust: Three options, worst to best: (1) keep this override and re-check the IP whenever the router changes; (2) add WiFi.config() to the sketch for a real static IP -- must sit OUTSIDE the router's DHCP pool or it will collide; (3) restore auto-discovery, which this project USED to have and lost in a refactor: the old POST /panic did `global ESP32_IP; ESP32_IP = request.client.host`, so the pole taught the backend its own address the first time its panic button was pressed. The current /api/panic_trigger dropped the `request: Request` parameter and no longer does this. Option 3 needs no IP configured anywhere and survives any DHCP change.

networking._fixed_2026-08-19: These were the Docker-compose-only 'backend' hostname, which does not resolve outside a compose network. Docker support (docker-compose.yml, which was the only thing overriding this to a real address for local runs) was removed from this repo -- so this JSON value is now what maincode/main.py actually uses whenever nothing overrides it, and every AI-triggered alert (violence/robbery/vandalism/weapons) was silently failing to reach the backend as a result. electron/main.js still overrides this correctly for the packaged desktop app (via the BACKEND_URL env var, now actually read -- see the matching comment in maincode/main.py), but a plain `python maincode/main.py` / run_dev_system.bat run had nothing to override it, so it needs to be correct here too.
